attachments.description: The files on the message. Empty when it has none or the message was deleted.

body.description: The message's text. Null when the message was deleted, or when it carries no text.

choices.description: The answers a workflow's question offers as buttons, each an id and a label. Send the tapped id as choice in the reply. Absent on any other message.

choices_only.description: True when the question can be answered only by tapping a choice, so hide the text box until one is tapped. Absent otherwise.

client_id.description: The client_id the visitor's client sent with this message, to match it with the copy shown while sending. Null for messages sent without one.

conversation_id.description: The id of the conversation the message belongs to, such as conv_abc123.

created_at.description: When it was created, as an RFC 3339 time, such as 2026-01-31T09:00:00Z.

deleted.description: True when the message was deleted: keep its place in the thread and show no body or files. Absent otherwise.

id.description: The id of this record. Send it wherever an endpoint asks for this record; never use its name or title in its place.

object.description: The kind of record this is, the same for every record of its kind, such as article.

read_at.description: When the message was read by the other side, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. Null while it is unread.

attachment_ids.description: Up to 10 ids of files this session finished uploading, such as ["att_4k2j9x"]; one that is missing, unfinished or another visitor's refuses the message.

body.description: The message text, such as "Where is my order?"; at most 64 KB, and required unless attachment_ids names a file.

choice.description: Id of the button the visitor tapped when the message answers a question drawn as buttons, up to 64 characters, so the workflow takes that path. Leave out otherwise.

client_id.description: A UUID the client makes up for this message, such as 6f1c2c1e-8a4b-4d1f-9c3e-2b7a5d9e0f11; sending the same one again returns the stored message instead of a second one.

context.description: Flat object of details the page passes along, such as {"plan": "pro"}: text, number or true/false values only, at most 30 keys and 4 KB, and null removes a key.

website.description: Hidden anti-bot form field that real visitors never fill, up to 1000 characters; leave it out or empty.

referrer.description: Address of the page that led here, such as https://google.com/; anything that is not an http or https address is dropped.

title.description: The page's title, such as Pricing; text beyond 300 characters is cut.

url.description: Full http or https address of the page, such as https://acme.com/pricing; kept up to 2048 characters, with query values that look like credentials removed.

custom_attributes.description: The contact's custom attributes as an object keyed by attribute name.

email.description: The visitor's email address as they or their app gave it. Null when none is known.

email_verified.description: True when the email address is confirmed as the visitor's own, false when it is only what they typed.

id.description: The id of this record. Send it wherever an endpoint asks for this record; never use its name or title in its place.

kind.description: user for a customer the host app signed in, lead for a visitor it has not.

locale.description: The visitor's language, such as en-US. Null when none is known.

name.description: The visitor's name as they or their app gave it. Null when none is known.

object.description: The kind of record this is, the same for every record of its kind, such as article.

phone.description: The visitor's phone number as they or their app gave it. Null when none is known.

name.description: Name of the client library, up to 64 characters, such as @dimmi/browser.

version.description: Version of the client library, up to 64 characters, such as 1.4.0.

config_version.description: The messenger's current settings version. When it is higher than the config you hold, fetch the config again.

expires_at.description: When the session stops working, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. Start a new session after that.

id.description: The id of this record. Send it wherever an endpoint asks for this record; never use its name or title in its place.

kind.description: anonymous for a visitor nobody signed in, identified for a customer verified with an identity token.

object.description: The kind of record this is, the same for every record of its kind, such as article.

open_conversation_ids.description: The ids of the visitor's conversations that are not closed, such as conv_abc123. Empty when there are none.

server_time.description: The server's clock when it answered, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

test.description: True for a test session, whose conversations are marked as test ones.

token.description: The session's secret, starting with dmi_ws_, to send as the bearer token on later calls. Present only on the answer that created the session, so store it then.

unread_count.description: How many of the team's replies the visitor has not read, across their conversations on this messenger.

conversation_id.description: The id of the conversation where the request is discussed, such as conv_abc123. Null when it has none.

created_at.description: When it was created, as an RFC 3339 time, such as 2026-01-31T09:00:00Z.

description.description: The longer explanation given when the request was opened. Empty when none was given.

fields.description: The request's fields a customer may see, each with its current value when it has one.

history.description: The states the request went through, each with its customer-facing label, its group and when it was entered.

id.description: The id of this record. Send it wherever an endpoint asks for this record; never use its name or title in its place.

mine.description: True when this visitor opened the request, false for a colleague's request their company shares.

object.description: The kind of record this is, the same for every record of its kind, such as article.

reference.description: The request's short reference as people quote it, such as T-482. It also works in place of the id when fetching the request.

resolved_at.description: When the request was resolved, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. Null while it is still open.

updated_at.description: When it last changed, as an RFC 3339 time, such as 2026-01-31T09:00:00Z.

id.description: The id of this record. Send it wherever an endpoint asks for this record; never use its name or title in its place.

reference.description: The request's short reference as people quote it, such as T-482.

currency.description: The three-letter currency code of a currency field, such as USD. Absent on other fields.

data_type.description: The kind of value: short_text, long_text, number, decimal, currency, boolean, date, single_choice, multiple_choice, file, member or company.

description.description: Help text explaining the field to the customer. Absent when it has none.

editable.description: True when the customer may change this field's value.

key.description: The field's stable name, used as the key in the fields object when opening a request, such as order_number.

label.description: The field's name as shown to the customer.

options.description: The values to pick from on a single_choice or multiple_choice field. Empty for other fields.

required.description: True when the customer must fill this field to open a request.

value.description: The field's current value on a request, shaped by its data_type. Absent on a type's form and when the request has no value for it.

at.description: When the request entered this state, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. Present only in a request's history.

group.description: The stage the state belongs to, which orders a progress strip: submitted, in_progress, waiting_customer, waiting_team or resolved.

label.description: The state's name as the customer reads it, never the team's internal name for it.

company_sharing.description: True when requests of this type are shared with the customer's colleagues at the same company.

description.description: A short explanation of what this type of request is for. May be empty.

fields.description: The form fields a customer fills when opening this type, in order. Empty when the type appears inside a request, whose own fields list holds them.

icon.description: The name of the icon the team picked for this type.

id.description: The id of this record. Send it wherever an endpoint asks for this record; never use its name or title in its place.

name.description: The type's name as shown to the customer, such as Bug report.

object.description: The kind of record this is, the same for every record of its kind, such as article.

states.description: The states a request of this type moves through, with their customer-facing labels. Empty when the type appears inside a request.

status.description: What became of the event: accepted, duplicate (its id was already sent), contact_not_found, archived, event_limit_reached or not_allowed.

accepted.description: How many events of the batch were accepted.

events.description: One result per event sent, in the same order as the request.

object.description: The kind of record this is, the same for every record of its kind, such as article.

id.description: The id of this record. Send it wherever an endpoint asks for this record; never use its name or title in its place.

links.description: Related addresses keyed by name. self is this upload's own address, which you PATCH with status uploaded once the bytes are sent.

object.description: The kind of record this is, the same for every record of its kind, such as article.

status.description: The upload's state. Always pending here, until you send the bytes and mark it uploaded.

expires_at.description: When the upload address stops working, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. Ask for a new upload after that.

headers.description: The headers to send with the upload exactly as given: Content-Type and Content-Length, matching what was declared.

method.description: The HTTP method to send the file's bytes with. Always PUT.

url.description: The address to send the file's bytes to: signed storage that takes them as they are, or dimmi's own upload route, which also needs the session's bearer token.

post.description: Tells dimmi that someone opened a help article inside the messenger, so the view is counted for the day. Needs no session: the messenger's app id goes in the path. Answers not found when the messenger links to no help center; an article the help center does not show is skipped without an error.

get.description: Tells whether someone on the team is there now and how soon they usually reply. Needs no session, only the messenger's app id, and the answer may be cached for 30 seconds. Returns the team's availability: online, within_hours, reply_time with its wording, team faces and the server time.

parameters.description: The messenger's app id from its install snippet, such as wgt_7h2k9d. An unknown, malformed or deleted id answers not found.
parameters.name: app

parameters.description: Language tag for the reply time wording, such as fr or pt-BR. Falls back to the base language, then English.
parameters.name: locale

get.description: Returns the newest published changelog entries of the help center this messenger links to, newest first, at most 20. Needs no session, only the app id in the path. The list is empty when the messenger has no help center or its changelog tab is off. Returns the full changelog's address and up to 20 entries with slug, title, summary, label, publish time and body blocks.

Returns everything a messenger needs to draw itself: appearance, texts in the visitor's language, tabs and settings. Call it first on every page load; it needs no session and is cacheable for a minute. Returns the messenger's config, or an empty 304 answer when If-None-Match matches the current version.

parameters.description: The messenger's app id from its install snippet, such as wgt_7h2k9d. An unknown, malformed or deleted id answers not found.
parameters.name: app

parameters.description: Language tag the visitor prefers, such as de or pt-BR. A messenger set to one fixed language ignores it, and English is the default.
parameters.name: locale

parameters.description: Any value, such as the config version 42. It is not read; it only keeps a CDN from answering with an older copy.
parameters.name: v

parameters.description: The Etag header of an earlier answer, sent back as is. When it still matches, the answer is 304 with no body.
parameters.name: If-None-Match

get.description: Returns the collections and published articles anyone may read in the help center this messenger links to, so help shows before the visitor says anything. Needs no session, only the app id in the path. Everything is empty when the messenger links to no help center. Returns the help center's address, its collections, up to 200 articles with body blocks, and up to 5 popular article slugs.

Lists the kinds of request a visitor may open from this messenger, so the home screen can offer them before the visitor writes. Needs no session, only the app id in the path. Returns the list of request types a customer may open.

post.description: Records whether a help article helped the visitor reading it in the messenger. Needs a messenger session and a help center linked to the messenger. Answering again changes the earlier answer instead of adding another.

Tells dimmi the visitor opened a help article inside the messenger, so the view is counted for the day; nothing about the visitor is kept with it. Needs a messenger session and a help center linked to the messenger.

First of three upload steps: say which file is coming and get back where to send its bytes. Needs a messenger session and a messenger with attachments switched on. Then send the bytes, mark the upload uploaded, and pass its id in attachment_ids. Returns the pending upload with its id, status and where to send the bytes.

patch.description: Last upload step: say the bytes arrived so dimmi checks them and marks the file uploaded. Needs the same messenger session that announced the file, and the bytes already sent. Returns the finished attachment, ready to name in attachment_ids.

parameters.description: Id of the upload this session announced, such as att_4k2j9x; any other id answers not found.
parameters.name: attachment

get.description: Returns what dimmi holds about the visitor behind the session. Needs a messenger session; the session decides whose profile it is, so no id is sent. Returns the visitor's profile.

patch.description: Lets a visitor say who they are: a name, an email to reply to, a phone number, a few attributes. Needs a messenger session. A signed-in customer's name, email and phone come from their app and are refused here; they may only write the attributes the workspace lets the messenger write. Returns the visitor's profile as it now is.

get.description: Lists the visitor's conversations on this messenger, latest activity first, a page at a time: 20 by default, 50 at most. Needs a messenger session. filter[status] narrows the list to open or closed conversations. Returns a page of the visitor's conversations with a cursor for the next page.

post.description: Starts a new conversation with the visitor's first message. Needs a messenger session; the messenger's rules may refuse the visitor, and a messenger that asks for an email while the team is away refuses a visitor without one. A session may start 5 conversations an hour. Returns the new conversation, with the stored message beside it.

get.description: Returns one of the visitor's conversations. Needs the messenger session it belongs to. Returns the conversation.

parameters.description: Id of one of the visitor's own conversations on this messenger, such as conv_8f3k2m; any other id answers not found.
parameters.name: conversation

get.description: Returns where an action the AI agent proposed in the conversation stands, to draw or refresh its confirmation card. Needs the messenger session the conversation belongs to. Returns the action call as the visitor sees it.

parameters.description: Id of one of the visitor's own conversations on this messenger, such as conv_8f3k2m; any other id answers not found.
parameters.name: conversation

parameters.description: Id of an action the agent proposed in this conversation, such as aax_5t8w2q; any other id answers not found.
parameters.name: call

patch.description: Records the visitor's yes or no to an action the AI agent proposed in the conversation. Needs the messenger session the conversation belongs to. Sending the same answer twice returns where the call stands and never runs anything twice. Returns the action call with its new state.

parameters.description: Id of one of the visitor's own conversations on this messenger, such as conv_8f3k2m; any other id answers not found.
parameters.name: conversation

parameters.description: Id of an action the agent proposed in this conversation, such as aax_5t8w2q; any other id answers not found.
parameters.name: call

get.description: Reads one conversation's messages a page at a time, oldest first within each page. Needs the messenger session the conversation belongs to. Use before to scroll back in history, or after to catch up from a message the client already holds. Returns a page of messages, with a cursor for older ones when more remain.

parameters.description: Id of one of the visitor's own conversations on this messenger, such as conv_8f3k2m; any other id answers not found.
parameters.name: conversation

parameters.description: The cursor a previous page returned, sent back as is, to read the messages older than that page.
parameters.name: before

parameters.description: Id of a message of this conversation the client already holds, such as msg_9d3f7a, to read the ones after it.
parameters.name: after

parameters.description: How many messages to return, 1 to 100, such as 50. Leaving it out, or 0, returns 30.
parameters.name: limit

post.description: Writes the visitor's message in a conversation. Needs the messenger session the conversation belongs to. A conversation closed long ago, or imported history, cannot take it: a new conversation does, and the answer names the old one in redirected_from. A session may send 20 messages a minute. Returns the stored message, with the conversation's status, whether it reopened and any redirect.

parameters.description: Id of one of the visitor's own conversations on this messenger, such as conv_8f3k2m; any other id answers not found.
parameters.name: conversation

get.description: Returns the latest request asking the visitor to rate the conversation, to draw the rating card. Needs the messenger session the conversation belongs to. Returns the conversation's latest rating request, or null when none was sent.

parameters.description: Id of one of the visitor's own conversations on this messenger, such as conv_8f3k2m; any other id answers not found.
parameters.name: conversation

patch.description: Saves the visitor's score and comment for a conversation that asked how it went. Needs the messenger session the conversation belongs to and an open rating request; answers not found without one. Send a score, a comment or both; they can be changed for a week after the request went out. Returns the rating with the visitor's answer.

parameters.description: Id of one of the visitor's own conversations on this messenger, such as conv_8f3k2m; any other id answers not found.
parameters.name: conversation

patch.description: Says how far the visitor read, so the team's replies up to that message count as read. Needs the messenger session the conversation belongs to. The pointer only moves forward: an older message changes nothing. Returns the read state with the count of replies still unread.

parameters.description: Id of one of the visitor's own conversations on this messenger, such as conv_8f3k2m; any other id answers not found.
parameters.name: conversation

post.description: Tells the team the visitor started or stopped typing in the conversation. Needs the messenger session the conversation belongs to. Nothing is stored, and repeated starts are thinned so teammates are not flooded.

parameters.description: Id of one of the visitor's own conversations on this messenger, such as conv_8f3k2m; any other id answers not found.
parameters.name: conversation

post.description: Mails a six-digit code to an address so an anonymous visitor can prove they own it. Needs an anonymous messenger session; a signed-in session is refused. The code works for 10 minutes, replaces any earlier one, and another may be sent after 30 seconds, up to 5 an hour per session. Returns the masked address, when the code expires and when another may be sent.

Takes the code the visitor typed. A good one marks the session's email proven for a day and the visitor's address verified. Needs the messenger session that asked for the code. Five wrong tries lock the code, and an expired code needs a new one. Returns the masked address and when it was verified.

Records what the visitor did on the page, up to 20 events at once, on the session's contact. Needs a messenger session. Only event names the workspace opened to the messenger are recorded, unless it lets the messenger send any; the server sets each event's time. A session may send 30 batches a minute. Returns what became of each event sent, such as accepted, duplicate or not_allowed.

get.description: Returns the help center's collections and articles as this visitor may read them: what their audiences open when the messenger knows them (signed in, or with a proven email), and what anyone may read otherwise. Needs a messenger session. Everything is empty when the messenger links to no help center. Returns the help center's address, its collections, up to 200 articles with body blocks, and up to 5 popular article slugs.

post.description: Returns the address to open an article, or the help center's home, in the full help center. Needs a messenger session and a help center linked to the messenger. A visitor the messenger knows gets an address that signs them in on arrival, good once and for a minute; anyone else gets the plain address. Returns the address to open.

Starts a conversation before the visitor has written anything, so a workflow can greet them the moment the chat opens. Needs a messenger session. The same limit as a first message applies, 5 new conversations an hour per session, and the messenger's rules may refuse the visitor. Returns the new, empty conversation.

Tells dimmi which page the visitor is on now, so the team sees where a question came from. Needs a messenger session. It is written down at most once every 10 seconds per session; faster pings are accepted and change nothing.

Issues a short-lived token that opens the visitor's live event stream. Needs a messenger session. Ask for a fresh one each time the stream opens or reopens: the token is good for about a minute and only for opening a stream, not for calling the API. Returns the connect token, when it expires, the stream's address and the visitor's channel.

delete.description: Signs the visitor out: the session's token stops working at once and its open streams close. Send the session token as a bearer token. Ending a session that already ended answers the same.

get.description: Returns the current session when a page loads with a stored token: who the visitor is, how many replies wait unread and which conversations are open. Works for anonymous sessions only; a signed-in session must send a fresh identity token with the session update instead. Returns the session, without its token.

patch.description: Proves a signed-in session's customer again with a fresh identity token, which extends the session and updates the customer from the token. Send the session token as a bearer token; an expired signed-in session is accepted here and revived. A token for anyone else is refused and the session stays as it was. Returns the session with its new expiry, without its token.

post.description: Starts a messenger session the first time a visitor does something, and returns the token every later request sends as Authorization: Bearer. Without user_jwt the session is anonymous, if the messenger allows that; with one the visitor is signed in once the token passes every check. A bad token is refused, never treated as anonymous. Returns the session with its token, shown only this once; a signed-in session that was extended instead comes back without one.

get.description: Lists the kinds of request the visitor may open from the messenger. Needs a messenger session. Use a type's id as type_id when opening a request. Returns the list of request types a customer may open.

Lists the requests the visitor opened, or their company's. Needs a messenger session. Company requests show only to a visitor signed in with a verified identity who belongs to a company, and only for request types shared with the company. Returns the list of requests as the customer sees them.

parameters.description: Whose requests to list: mine for the visitor's own, or company for their company's too. Leaving it out means mine.
parameters.name: scope

parameters.description: true to keep only requests not yet resolved, such as open=true. Leaving it out lists all of them.
parameters.name: open

post.description: Submits a request form: dimmi checks it, starts a conversation with the title and description as the visitor's first message, and puts a ticket on it. Needs a messenger session. Replies then go through that conversation's messages; the same client_id sent twice makes one request. Returns the request as the customer sees it.

get.description: Returns one of the visitor's requests with the states it went through. Needs a messenger session. Returns the request with its state history.

parameters.description: The request's id, such as tkt_6b2n8r, or its reference, such as T-482 or 482.
parameters.name: ticket

get.description: Polling fallback for clients whose live stream is blocked: returns what changed in the visitor's conversations since the last poll, at most 100 changes. Needs a messenger session. Each answer carries the cursor for the next poll and how long to wait; when has_more is true, poll again at once. Returns the changes since the cursor, with the next cursor, the wait before the next poll and whether more remain.

parameters.description: The cursor from the previous answer's meta, sent back as is. Leave it out on the first poll.
parameters.name: since
